subject: VAL
label: Grade 04
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 04 Values and life skills, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Honesty and trust
modules.outcome: explain why trust takes time to build
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Honesty and trust', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: explain why trust takes time to build. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen and talk: hear a short story, text or example linked to 'Honesty and trust' and say what it means in your own words.
Connect: name one place in your own day where it applies.
Use it: explain why trust takes time to build. Practise with care and respect, in class and at home.
Reflect: what went well, what was hard, and one thing you will do next time.
modules.example: Solved: You break a cup. Honest action: tell the adult straight away, say what happened and offer to help clean. Trust grows when we tell the truth even when it is hard. Method: Model run for 'Honesty and trust'. A short text or story is read aloud. Learners say the main lesson in one sentence. In pairs they find one moment in school or home where this lesson would help. Each learner plans one small action for the week and tells it to a partner. At the end of the week they report back. What a good answer looks like: the lesson is in the learner's own words, the example is real and local, and the action is small enough to do. Content follows the approved local syllabus and is checked by a qualified teacher.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Explain why trust takes time to build: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.

steps: Step 1, listen to or read the short text for 'Compassion'. Say the main lesson in one sentence.
Step 2, link it: describe one real moment this week where it applies.
Step 3, plan one small action you can do in two days.
Step 4, do it with care and respect for others.
Step 5, reflect: what went well, what was hard, what did you learn?
Step 6, share one sentence with a partner and listen to theirs. Standard: describe how to help someone who is sad or hurt. Content follows the approved local syllabus.

FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36.

What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
One page in your learning book. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard.
ladder: L1: kindness, honesty and sharing in daily life.
L2: responsibility, courage and care for others and nature.
L3: fairness, respect for difference and service.
L5: leadership, wellbeing and ethical reasoning.
L6 (degree): applied ethics, culture and community work.
L7 (postgraduate): scholarship, counselling or teaching at depth.
